newsitem.title: DENMARK: Quiet Danish bonds slip slightly ahead of US data.
newsitem.headline: Quiet Danish bonds slip slightly ahead of US data.

text.p: Danish bond prices fell a tad on Friday in a quiet market with focus on the afternoon's welter of U.S. data and the 10-year yield gap with Germany stable.
"There has been a little nervousness ahead of the U.S figures but the market is basically quiet with the 10-year yield gap holding at around 50 basis points," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.04 point from the opening at 114.21, yielding 5.84 percent, while the seven percent 2007 paper, which becomes the benchmark on September 1, shed 0.08 point to 107.22, with the yield at 6.03 percent.
Turnover in the tone-setting 2006 and 2007 benchmarks was 930 million and 470 million crowns respectively.
The 2006's September future was untraded at 114.06. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.20 point to 93.25.
The crown traded at 3.8110 per mark at 1100 GMT, down from around 3.8095 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 50 basis points from the start of trading.
